title: Design System: Otto 在线编舞台

bed.purpose: The cover only: the 8px page edge, the 44px header strip, the two footer lines. It is never a working surface.

ivory.purpose: The sheet: the left panel ground, the 3D stage ground, the selected frame row, the modal. The robot stands on the same paper the sliders are printed on.

carbon.purpose: The printed block: the right column only (frame table, meter, code strip). #26221A is the second carbon used inside that column's inputs.

vermilion.purpose: States that move or destroy: the playing row's fill (#8F2A12), the ruler cursor, the current frame's rail tick, the danger hover, the warning line. Never a background for body text.

bottle.purpose: The confirmed connection: the 8px dot only. At 3.29:1 on the cover it clears the 3:1 UI-graphic bar but not the text bar, so the status word beside it stays carbon.

ui.purpose: Every label, value and heading, set in Archivo Narrow (embedded base64 woff2, latin subset, 400/700). Measured 10x'M' at 13px = 88.80px; the Arial fallback would be 108.30px.

ui-mobile.purpose: The same single size raised for a phone held at arm's length.

data.purpose: The sequence JSON. A different substance from a label, so it gets the mono stack at 11.5px.

data-inline.purpose: Angle pairs inside frame rows and the refdes chips beside each axis name.

shadows.name: contact-shadow
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the design, and it is cast by light, not drawn by CSS: the robot's real shadow on the cream page is what holds a white model on a light ground.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Two-tone, because one colour cannot survive two substances: ivory ring 14.62:1 on carbon, carbon halo 11.35:1 on the sheet. A single vermilion ring measured only 1.79:1 on the cover.

motion.name: state-fill
motion.purpose: Button, preset and row hover/active fills.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: The only element that moves on its own.

gradients.name: servo-scale
gradients.value: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(28,25,19,.45) 0 1px, transparent 1px 15px) over a 1px rule
gradients.purpose: A graduation scale for 0–180°, one tick every 15°. Functional measurement, not decoration.

gradients.name: ruler-scale
gradients.value: repeating-linear-gradient major every 50px / minor every 10px at rgba(28,25,19,.42) and .20
gradients.purpose: The graduation under the stage, now drawn in carbon on paper because the stage is the paper.

breakpoints.name: desk-narrow
breakpoints.note: Columns tighten; the rack narrows with the viewport.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.note: One stack, stage first via order:-1; hairline dividers become block bottom edges.

breakpoints.name: captions
breakpoints.note: The stage's right-hand caption drops out and the two cover footers wrap instead of colliding.

breakpoints.name: handheld
breakpoints.note: Type 13→15px, 42px touch targets, frame actions wrap under their row.

components.name: Section Head
components.description: Uppercase tracked title with a right-aligned micro tag, separated by a single hairline. No background, no box.

components.name: Servo Row
components.description: One axis: name, reversed mono key chip, value, a ticked track with a 3px bar thumb, and the range description under it. Side is carried by the name and the chip only — the right-side vermilion value was removed because on paper it read as an alarm.

components.name: Pose Cell
components.description: A printed table cell in a two-column grid, not a button: no border box, no fill, no radius. Name in 700, the number set in the cell's top-right corner, the description beneath in secondary ink.

components.name: Frame Table Head
components.description: The row that makes the rack a timetable instead of a stack: 帧 / 类型 / 参数 · v / d, one hairline thick, in secondary silk.

components.name: Frame Row
components.description: A table row, not a card. Mono index, type label (振荡 in goldenrod), one line of mono angle pairs with the timing after it, actions flush right behind hairlines. Selection reverses the whole row to an ivory sheet; previewing fills it with #8F2A12.

components.name: Tick Rail
components.description: A 16px index column beside the frame table: one tick per frame, the current one wider and vermilion. Each tick is drawn by its own row so it cannot drift.

components.name: Ruler + Playhead
components.description: A 26px graduated strip under the stage, drawn in carbon on paper with the stage. The playhead chip is a goldenrod tab riding it.

components.name: Page Caption
components.description: Printed on the page rather than floating over it: the stage's two top corners and the line under the viewport that declares the projection, the grid and the servo limits.

narrative.northStar: 封面里的奶油纸时刻表 — The Pocket Timetable, Bound
narrative.overview:
The tool is a 1971 pocket timetable printed on a cream sheet and glued into a goldenrod hard cover. The cover is the frame you hold — an 8px edge, a 44px header strip, two mono footer lines. The sheet is the page you fill in, and it is continuous: six axes and a sixteen-pose library on the left, the robot standing on the same paper in the centre, divided only by hairlines. The right column is the one block printed in dark ink: frame table, meter, code strip.

Two substances, paper and ink, plus a cover. That is the whole system. One type size; rank from weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule. One radius: zero. No elevation, no icon set, no gradient used as surface treatment. Every colour names a job — cover, sheet, printed ink, reversal, armed, confirmed — and a colour that cannot name its job is decoration and does not ship.

The first build of this world got the ground backwards: it treated the goldenrod as the field and made the stage carbon, so the page read as a dark tool with gold trim rather than a cream timetable in a gold cover. The correction is the point of the system: paper is the working surface, gold is the binding, and the only dark thing is the block that was printed.
keyCharacteristics: Ivory sheet carrying the panels and the 3D stage alike — the robot stands on the same paper the sliders are printed on
Goldenrod only as the binding: 8px page edge, header strip, two footer lines
One dark printed block on the right, running the full height of the page
The frame rack is a table: a named header row, four fixed columns, hairline rows
Rank by weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule — never by size
Drawn scales: a ticked slider track and a graduated ruler, both in carbon on paper
One real shadow: the robot's own, cast by the key light onto the page

rules.name: Cover Is Visible Rule
rules.body: The goldenrod is binding, not background. It appears only as the page edge, the header strip and the footer lines, and it must be visible on all four sides. Spending it as a panel fill turns the cover into a field and inverts the world.

rules.name: Paper Stage Rule
rules.body: The stage is the sheet, not a dark box. A white robot on cream is held by a real contact shadow and a faint 280-unit grid; putting it back on carbon makes it a different product with the same widgets.

rules.name: One Size Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one type size, 13px (15px below 600px). Hierarchy is spent on weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule. Adding a second size is the fastest way to make this interface look like the generic tool it replaced.

rules.name: Named Job Rule
rules.body: Six hues, six jobs: gold is the cover, ivory is the sheet, carbon is the printed block, vermilion is a moving or destructive state, bottle green is the confirmed dot. A colour without a job is decoration.

rules.name: Solid Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on the cover uses solid ink (#1C1913 primary, #3A2C08 secondary), never an alpha tint. Alpha over a saturated ground cannot hold AA at any comfortable lightness.

rules.name: Table Rule
rules.body: The frame rack is one table: a header row naming the columns, four fixed column widths, a hairline under every row, and a tick rail down the left edge. Rows are never cards — no border box, no gap, no sheared edge.

rules.name: No Elevation Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats and nothing has a blur. Depth is binding order — cover, sheet, printed block — and selection is a reversed sheet cut into the dark block.

rules.name: No Side Stripe Rule
rules.body: State is a filled row, a reversed sheet, or a drawn rule. An accent bar down one edge of a row or a toast is the generic pattern this world is trying to escape.

rules.name: Instrument Rule
rules.body: A drawn instrument must print real data. The playhead shows the true frame count at rest, the ruler cursor sits at activeFrame/(n-1), and each rail tick is drawn by its own row so it cannot drift.

dos: Keep the goldenrod binding visible on all four sides of the sheet
Print the stage captions on the page instead of floating chrome over it
Spend rank on weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule first
Draw a scale whenever a number has a range
Give the selected frame row the ivory reversal and nothing else
Print the row number in the margin (R1–R6, P01–P16) when a head promises a count
Use the mono stack only for machine output, timings and inline axis tokens
donts: Add a second type size for hierarchy
Turn the stage back into a carbon box
Round a corner, lift a row, or add a blurred shadow
Let the frame table drift apart into floating cards
Use a gradient as surface decoration
Reintroduce an icon set — labels are the icons
Use an alpha tint for text on the cover
